incidents.vector: An unspecified intrusion into Rosstat's IT systems disrupted the agency's ability to publish data; a Belarusian opposition hacktivist collective claimed responsibility.
incidents.impact: Russia's statistics agency failed to publish scheduled weekly price data and other economic reports, with delays expected to continue through at least Nov. 13, and some previously published data disappeared from the agency's website.

incidents.victim: Italian government officials, including the foreign minister's office
incidents.vector: An unspecified cyberattack, attributed by Italian officials to pro-Russian hackers, compromised government systems tied to the foreign minister's office.
incidents.impact: Confidential information concerning Italian government officials was reportedly offered for sale online; Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni linked the incident to a rise in hybrid disruptions from Russia-aligned actors.

incidents.victim: Financial-sector organizations in Southeast Asia and globally
incidents.vector: The actor combined an agentic AI offensive framework with conventional scanning tools to exploit flaws such as anonymous file upload and server-side request forgery, then installed open-source remote access trojans for persistence.
incidents.impact: Compromised financial institutions faced automated brute-force password attacks, API abuse, database dumping, and lateral movement conducted largely by AI agents with minimal hands-on-keyboard activity, expanding from a Southeast Asia focus to a smaller number of large global financial firms.

incidents.victim: Multiple companies across healthcare, finance, and technology sectors
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — financial fraud using AI deepfakes
incidents.vector: Three men used AI-generated voice and video deepfakes to impersonate company CEOs and law-firm attorneys, directing accounting staff to wire funds for purported confidential transactions.
incidents.impact: The scheme defrauded victims of at least $129 million between 2024 and 2026, including a U.K. fintech, a Florida pet-food company, hospital systems in Missouri and California, a Massachusetts mutual fund firm, a New York investment company, and a Rhode Island bank; all three defendants have been arrested and indicted in the U.S.

incidents.vector: An unspecified intrusion into the French banking group's systems enabled theft of funds, later traced through on-chain laundering activity.
incidents.impact: Hackers stole $133 million from the French banking group; blockchain investigators identified the theft this week after the stolen funds began moving through laundering channels.

incidents.vector: An internal business system was inadvertently left externally accessible after a February 2025 network migration, allowing an unassigned account to be created and used to access a customer database starting June 27, 2026.
incidents.impact: Customer names, business emails, phone numbers, and identity documents such as driver's licenses and passports were exposed; DigiCert says certificate-issuance capability and login credentials were not affected.

incidents.vector: Attackers used AI tools to speed up and automate an intrusion into the blockchain hosting platform's systems.
incidents.impact: Customer data was stolen from Chainstack in an incident that took place at the end of October; the company has not disclosed the scope of affected accounts.

incidents.vector: A senior FBI counterintelligence agent used his authorized access to investigative systems holding seized cryptocurrency wallet credentials to conduct roughly 100 fraudulent transfers across 35 separate investigations.
incidents.impact: The agent stole more than $2.4 million in cryptocurrency from wallets tied to nation-state and criminal investigations, compromising sources and methods across multiple FBI cases; he pleaded guilty to wire fraud and money laundering and faces up to 20 years.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the internal network of Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs; the method of entry was not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Data on 3,600 ministry employees, including names and email addresses, was stolen in an intrusion that took place at the end of July; the ministry says the secure portion of its network was not affected.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached Norad's network via 27 compromised accounts.
incidents.impact: Personal data belonging to more than 20,000 grant applicants was stolen; Norad is working with Norway's National Security Authority to investigate.

incidents.vector: An attacker used a stolen employee credential to access systems lacking multi-factor authentication; poorly configured monitoring software recorded but did not flag the intrusion for two months.
incidents.impact: Names, Social Security numbers, diagnoses, medications, and other health data for more than 13 million people were exposed in a March 2023 breach; the company agreed to pay $300,000 and overhaul its security program, or face $9.7 million in added penalties if it fails to comply.

incidents.victim: Executive Office of the President (White House)
incidents.vector: White House staff devices had residential-proxy apps installed via bundled SDKs in free mobile and desktop software, including one tied to a Russian founder, which rent out device bandwidth and IP addresses to third parties.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed 236 proxy exit events from the White House's dedicated network over roughly a month via at least 28 different residential-proxy services, exposing the network to potential abuse by unknown third-party renters.

incidents.victim: Li Auto electric vehicle owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Attackers took over master user accounts on Li Auto smart EVs — most registered with Chinese eSIMs provided by importers — to lock owners out of their vehicles.
incidents.impact: At least 20 confirmed Li Auto owners in Russia had their vehicles hijacked and were extorted to regain control; the actual number of affected vehicles is believed to be higher.

incidents.victim: Supermarket chains and blood banks across Europe
incidents.vector: Attackers exploited internet-exposed refrigeration controllers (Danfoss, Dixell, and Copeland XWEB systems) with weak or default credentials to force units into continuous defrost and heating cycles.
incidents.impact: A second wave of attacks spread from roughly 700 French supermarkets to over 100 additional retail locations across at least 10 European countries; Ahold Delhaize alone expects up to €250 million in lost sales, and refrigeration at French blood banks was also targeted, though no plasma was lost. Pro-Russian groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest claimed credit, though attribution remains unverified.

incidents.victim: Owners of Android TV set-top boxes and other IoT devices worldwide
incidents.attacker: China — commercial device manufacturer, financially motivated
incidents.vector: A Chinese device manufacturer, Videostrong Technology Co., built backdoor malware into Android TV boxes that enrolled devices into a botnet and sold access to residential-proxy resellers and other criminal affiliates.
incidents.impact: More than 1.3 million Android TV boxes were infected and used for ad fraud and bandwidth resale; Google and industry partners dismantled the botnet's infrastructure, which also risked exposing an additional 10 million connected IoT devices including telehealth devices.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency platforms including Flap, Kintsu, Pickle Finance, and Origami Finance
incidents.vector: An attacker compromised a customer support account at domain registrar Name.com and used it to redirect at least 15 cryptocurrency-related domains to phishing sites.
incidents.impact: Customer wallets connected through the hijacked domains were drained in an incident that took place on October 31.

incidents.vector: Russian-linked hackers breached the Ukrainian news outlet's content management system.
incidents.impact: The attackers sent a fraudulent newsletter containing false claims that President Zelensky had been shot and that he had launched a nuclear weapon against Kyiv.

incidents.vector: Attackers weaponized a crypto-wallet feature that lets an account grant software standing permission to move funds, draining roughly 40% of the stolen assets in a single transaction that cost about $15 to execute.
incidents.impact: Roughly $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen in the largest crypto theft on record, spanning 11 different tokens; about $2.8 billion was later frozen, leaving over $3.25 billion unrecoverable. The FBI attributed the theft to a North Korean hacking group it tracks as TraderTraitor.

incidents.victim: Foreign ministries, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, and telecommunications organizations across 14+ countries
incidents.vector: The actor used an agentic AI framework paired with Chinese and commercial large language models to run intrusions against more than 200 organizations in parallel, chaining vulnerabilities such as unsigned SAML assertions and XXE flaws to reach cloud and on-premises systems.
incidents.impact: Confirmed post-exploitation activity occurred at nine organizations including foreign ministries in Latin America and the Middle East, two U.S. pharmaceutical companies, and government entities in Europe, with a custom backdoor deployed and data likely exfiltrated at several sites.

incidents.victim: Space and satellite services, defense/aerospace technology, and policy research organizations
incidents.vector: The actor exploited an authentication bypass vulnerability in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances to gain unauthorized access, then installed a custom malware framework to intercept decrypted control-plane traffic and harvest encryption keys.
incidents.impact: The intrusions provided long-term persistent access to SD-WAN controller environments and automated exfiltration of sensitive network encryption keys; the operator's infrastructure overlaps with a known China state-linked covert access network.

incidents.vector: The actor conducted a large-scale password-spraying campaign against more than 340 primarily U.S.-based organizations, directing nearly 500 distinct login attempts at a single law firm from roughly 300 different IP addresses over 30 days.
incidents.impact: The campaign represented the largest-scale operation by target count observed against the legal sector, reflecting intensified China-linked espionage targeting of law firms' privileged client and case data.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached government IT systems and began extracting data before being detected by government IT staff.
incidents.impact: Data on roughly a third of Moldova's population was stolen; officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach, in one of the country's worst cybersecurity incidents to date.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime, and global shipping companies
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware and data extortion
incidents.vector: The group compromised a South Korean maritime IT services provider and pivoted from that single access point into dozens of its port authority and shipping-company customers.
incidents.impact: More than 40 maritime and port organizations were listed on the group's dark web leak site after a payment deadline expired on Oct. 19; roughly half of the victims are known customers of the same IT services provider.
